chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, the people of Makkah, when they depart as pilgrims, they shorten (their prayers), and when they visit (the Kaaba) and return to their homes, they complete (their prayers).

key_terms.أَهْلَ مَكَّةَ: People of Makkah / Residents of Makkah

ai.seo_question: Do residents of Makkah shorten their prayers during Hajj or pray fully?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the jurisprudential distinction for Makkah's residents regarding prayer length, emphasizing that the obligation to shorten (Qasr) applies specifically to the state of Hajj travel, whereas visiting for Umrah or returning home does not trigger this reduction. It highlights the Shia scholarly view that the 'traveler' status is defined by the purpose and nature of the journey, distinguishing between the ritualistic travel of Hajj and the local movement of Umrah or return. This ruling underscores the practical application of travel laws in the holy city, ensuring worshippers adhere to the correct prayer format based on their specific religious intent.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The inhabitants of Makkah, when they exit as pilgrims, would shorten (their Salaat), and when they visit (the Kabah) and return to their houses, (would Pray) complete’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

If people of Makkah come out as Hajj (pilgrims) they perform their Salat (prayer) in Taqsir (reduced Salat (prayer) as on a journey after traveling a certain distance), but when they visit and return to their lodging they perform complete.’” NOTE: Fatwa best explains Hadith 1-2 of this Chapter
